summary.headline: Tonbo Imaging H1 FY27 revenue INR219 crore, with Q2 at INR183 crore driving the half; management guides H2 "materially better" but no numeric guidance.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR219 crore versus INR77 crore in H1 FY26, with Q2 at INR183 crore against Q1 at INR36 crore. Gross margin was INR75 crore (34.62%), below FY26's 51%, which management attributed to product mix. EBITDA was INR31.15 crore (14.2% margin) for H1 and INR44 crore (24.11%) for Q2, with employee cost largely fixed across quarters. Management stressed that performance should be judged annually, not by quarter or half, given that FY26 was 78% H2-weighted.

segments.name: Tactical systems
segments.commentary: Thermal weapon sights, binoculars and similar soldier-carried products; management says these are 70-80% of business. Domestic gross margin is about 40-45%. About INR250 crore of the INR408 crore contracts under negotiation are tactical.

segments.name: Platform systems
segments.commentary: Gimbals, fire control systems, weapon stations and seekers; domestic gross margin about 45-50%. Order book of INR250 crore is said to be about INR200 crore platform in an analyst's framing, which management confirmed includes both legacy and newer products. About INR150 crore of contracts under negotiation are platform.

segments.name: Directed energy (HPM)
segments.commentary: Still in development at TRL 4. Five Indian Navy and six European LOIs (11 units total). Expected first delivery 2029-30; first system cost about INR160 crore, funded by EXIM loan (INR120 crore sanctioned), iDEX ADITI grant (INR25 crore) and internal accruals (INR15 crore).

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; company cites recent IPO as a constraint.
Management expects H2 FY27 revenue to be materially higher than H1, and EBITDA margin to exceed H1's 14.2% on higher revenue and export mix.
Order book INR250 crore plus contracts under negotiation INR408 crore; management expects contracts under negotiation to convert by December, allowing revenue in FY27.
Management indicated INR100-200 crore of execution this year from OCPP and related orders, with the excess rolling into FY28.
R&D spend in H2 expected at about INR30 crore total, of which about INR25 crore capitalised (excluding HPM); H1 R&D about INR16 crore with INR3 crore expensed.
capex_capacity: Company is fabless and manufactures through certified partners, so capex is directed to design and IP rather than plants.
HPM directed energy first system: project cost about INR160 crore (hard cost ~INR120 crore; soft cost including ~INR20 crore capitalised employee cost over 2.5 years).
Tactical sub-assemblies held in inventory allow tactical orders to convert to revenue in three to four months if placed by December.
Platform deliveries take 6-18 months from order; tactical deliveries 3-6 months generally.
Bank cash credit being increased with the other two banks following the INR50 crore increase from one bank.
demand_pricing: Export loitering munition programme: first production order from a European state-owned company for multi-sensor stabilised seeker; option for up to EUR13 million after acceptance of FOPM units. Management said this option is included in the INR408 crore contracts under negotiation, not the INR250 crore order book.

India tactical opportunity: about 80,000 thermal weapon sights and handheld thermal imagers and about 27,000 image intensifiers in stated requirement; management expects 75,000 thermal sights, 5,000 thermal imagers, and 27,000 image intensifiers in the near-term tactical slide. International near-term opportunity about 10,000 thermal sights and monoculars.
Management claims about 65% share of the ~30,000 Indian thermal weapon sights deployed (20,000 from Tonbo) and expects to hold roughly 50% in future programmes.
Two-thirds of Q2 export-related commentary: an analyst noted INR51.5 crore Q2 revenue from the US; management confirmed these are platform subsystems but declined to name customers.
Competitors in India named as Bharat Electronics, Tata and Alpha Design; BEL Optronic Devices cited as not competing on the Arjun RCWS EO system.

qa_highlights.question: How do directed energy TAM figures reconcile (USD290 million by 2030 vs INR28,000 crore across 140 systems)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR28,000 crore (140 systems at about INR200 crore each) is the overall Indian market size, while USD290 million corresponds to the FY2030 expected figure, not the total market.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin differences between tactical and platform, domestic and export?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic tactical gross margin about 40-45%, domestic platform 45-50%, and exports 60-65% without a tactical/platform split.

qa_highlights.question: How long does conversion from order book to revenue take?
qa_highlights.answer: Tactical deliveries take 3-6 months from order, or about 3 months if long-lead items are in stock; platform deliveries take 6-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book alone deliver H1-level revenue in H2, and what is the year-end order book target?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said contracts under negotiation should convert by December, and that INR100-200 crore could be executed this year from OCPP and similar orders, with the remainder carried into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How does competition from BEL Optronic Devices and others affect Tonbo?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tonbo's full IP ownership across the thermal sight value chain gives it an edge over Bharat Electronics, Tata and Alpha Design, while expecting its share to fall from about 65% to around 50%.

qa_highlights.question: How are R&D and HPM costs accounted for and capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 R&D was about INR16 crore with about INR3 crore expensed; H2 total R&D about INR30 crore with about INR25 crore capitalised, excluding HPM. HPM total project cost is about INR160 crore, not all a P&L debit.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness: Q1 was INR36 crore and Q2 INR183 crore; management expects H2 to be materially higher but gives no number, and H2 relies on contracts under negotiation converting by December.
Platform programmes depend on partner vehicle, vessel and aircraft readiness, which can shift revenue between quarters.
HPM directed energy: TRL 4 with first delivery 2029-30; funding relies on an EXIM loan of INR120 crore and iDEX grant.
Gross margin fell to 34.62% in H1 from 51% in FY26 on mix; sustained recovery is needed for the H2 margin improvement management is pointing to.
Working-capital dependence: bank borrowings INR169 crore, with cash credit limits being raised at banks.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term market direction and product position, but cautious and non-committal on near-term numbers: management declined revenue and margin guidance, citing the recent IPO, and repeatedly asked investors to judge the business annually.
key_quotes: Products-based defense businesses like ours need to be looked at from the lens of a three -to-five-year perspective, and our business performance tracked on an annual basis.
While we are not giving a revenue guidance at this stage, we believe that H2 revenues for this financial year are likely to be materially better than H1.
We will keep investin g in directed energy over the next three to four years. You need to treat this as an option that we are building, not a short -term revenue.

Our model is completely different. We are a product company, and our emphasis is that the technology specs that we can create based on our experience selling these products to international customers is far superior to what comes out today as part of localized specs.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Fabless model means no utilisation-driven plant capex; the only announced spend is HPM (about INR160 crore, TRL 4), already funded by EXIM loan INR120 crore, iDEX grant INR25 crore and accruals INR15 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance given, citing the recent IPO; if December conversions of INR408 crore negotiations land, management could firm up numbers, but the company has not offered any figure yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue is lumpy (Q1 INR36 crore vs Q2 INR183 crore), H2 depends on December conversion, and platform deliveries take 6-18 months; the company has given no numbers to miss.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch dated in the window; HPM is at TRL 4 with first delivery 2029-30.

rows.label: Contracts under negotiation convert by December
rows.why: INR408 crore under negotiation (about INR250 crore tactical, INR150 crore platform) expected to convert by December; tactical converts to revenue in 3-4 months, so most would land in FY27 H2.

rows.label: Export loitering munition production order
rows.why: First production order from a European state-owned company, with an option up to EUR13 million after FOPM acceptance; the option sits in the INR408 crore under negotiation, not the INR250 crore order book.

rows.label: Bank cash credit limits being raised
